hooks.text: Every NASA shuttle landing was technically an unpowered emergency.
Space shuttles never used their engines to actually land.
An 80-ton spacecraft landed 135 times without any engine power.

title: Every Shuttle Landing Was an Emergency
description: The Space Shuttle was the world's heaviest glider, completing all 135 landings without any engine power.

beats.text: Every NASA shuttle landing was technically an unpowered emergency.
beats.visual: Space Shuttle landing on a runway with drag chute deployed, 1982
queries: Space Shuttle landing Edwards Air Force Base drag chute

beats.text: Most people imagine the engines roaring as the ship touches down.
beats.visual: Astronaut flight deck inside a Space Shuttle cockpit, 1995
queries: Space Shuttle Atlantis glass cockpit MEDS display

beats.text: But once the deorbit burn finished, those engines stayed completely silent.
beats.visual: Space Shuttle main engines deorbit burn in space, 1984
queries: Space Shuttle main engines deorbit burn

beats.text: The 80-ton orbiter fell toward Earth as a massive, unpowered glider.
beats.visual: Shuttle Carrier Aircraft carrying test orbiter Enterprise, 1977
queries: Space Shuttle Enterprise ALT test flight

beats.text: Thermal tiles reached 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit while screaming through the air.
beats.visual: Thermal protection system heat tiles on the underside of an orbiter, 1981
queries: Space Shuttle thermal protection system tiles
Space Shuttle heat shield tiles underside

beats.text: With no engines for a second attempt, any miss meant total loss.
beats.visual: Space Shuttle Atlantis landing after final mission STS-135, 2011

beats.text: Between 1981 and 2011, five orbiters performed this feat 135 times.
beats.visual: Stacked Space Shuttle Endeavour exhibit with external tank and boosters, 2012
queries: Space Shuttle Endeavour stacked exhibit California Science Center
Space Shuttle stack external tank boosters

beats.text: They proved every landing could be handled as an unpowered emergency.
beats.visual: Space Shuttle Discovery on runway after landing, 1998
